task_instance: Apply the Hootsuite SDK patterns from the skill to produce the four stated deliverables as real project files: a typed TypeScript API client (SocialProfile/ScheduledMessage/HootsuiteResponse interfaces), timezone-aware scheduling helpers (scheduleForTimezone + OPTIMAL_TIMES), a cross-platform post formatter (platform character-limit truncation), and a Python HootsuiteClient class; then verify them by strict type-checking/compiling the TypeScript and running the pure helpers, and by compiling/importing/constructing the Python client.
evidence: Wrote src/hootsuite/{types,scheduling,formatter}.ts and hootsuite/client.py in the work directory matching the skill's code patterns. Installed TypeScript 5.6.3 locally (node_modules); 'npx tsc --noEmit' under strict mode -> TYPECHECK_OK, 'npx tsc' emitted dist/{types,scheduling,formatter}.js plus .d.ts declaration files. Ran dist/test.mjs with node: scheduleForTimezone(LinkedIn 07:30, +1 day) produced a valid ISO date 2026-11-01T07:30:00.000Z; formatPost truncated a 300-char string to exactly 280 chars with trailing ellipsis for TWITTER, left an 11-char INSTAGRAM string untouched, and applied the 2200 fallback for an unknown platform -> TS_RUNTIME_TESTS_PASS. For Python: created .venv in the work directory, installed requests (2.34.2) and python-dotenv, 'python -m py_compile hootsuite/client.py' -> PY_COMPILE_OK, imported the module and constructed HootsuiteClient with a dummy local env token -> correct Bearer Authorization and application/json Content-Type headers and get_profiles/schedule_message methods present (PY_CLIENT_CONSTRUCT_OK). The skill is a code-pattern/standards skill (allowed-tools Read/Write/Edit); its core deliverable is the idiomatic client/helper/formatter code, which was produced and verified. Only live calls against the real Hootsuite REST endpoint would additionally need an access token and network reach (the base URL was a placeholder in the source), but that is outside the skill's stated deliverable and was not required.
